issues.t: Sudden loss of drive power from battery software (recall)
issues.sym: The car can lose drive power while moving, sometimes after a high-voltage battery warning. Steering and brakes still work, but the car coasts to a stop.
issues.why: Other computers in the car flooded the battery management unit with diagnostic requests until its memory overflowed, and it then disconnected the drive battery. Recall 24V-372 covers 2024 EQE sedans and 2023–2025 EQE SUVs, including AMG versions.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have a Mercedes dealer check your VIN and install the free battery software update. It cannot be done over the air.

issues.sym: You may notice looseness, clunking or vague steering. In the worst case steering control can be lost.
issues.why: The bolt joining the steering shaft coupling to the steering rack may not have been tightened properly at the factory, so the coupling can work loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-533 right away. The dealer tightens the bolt free. If the steering feels loose, don't drive the car.

issues.sym: Without warning, the car may lose drive power, or safety systems like the airbags and instrument cluster may stop working.
issues.why: 80-amp fuses in the main fuse box may have been made incorrectly and can fail. A failing fuse can also raise the risk of a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-115. The dealer replaces the main fuse boxes free.

issues.t: Wrong fuse box installed during earlier repair (recall)
issues.sym: The same symptoms as the fuse recall: sudden loss of drive power or of safety systems such as airbags and the instrument cluster.
issues.why: Some cars fixed under recall 24V-115 were given a fuse box that was not designed for them.
issues.next: Even if the fuse recall was done, check your VIN for recall 25V-255. The dealer inspects and replaces the fuse boxes free.

issues.t: Drivetrain software can cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: The car may suddenly lose power while driving, usually with a drivetrain warning message.
issues.why: A software error in the electric drivetrain control can shut off propulsion. In the EQE line this recall covers the 2023 AMG EQE.
issues.next: Have the dealer install the drivetrain software update under recall 23V-405. It is free.

issues.t: Wheel rim inserts can come off (recall)
issues.sym: There are usually no signs. A decorative insert in the wheel may fly off while driving.
issues.why: The rim inserts on some 2023 EQE 350 sedans may not be fixed firmly enough to the wheel to stay on under driving forces.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-150. The dealer inspects the inserts and replaces them if needed, free.

issues.sym: The headlights may light the road poorly or dazzle oncoming drivers.
issues.why: A software error in the headlight control unit can set the wrong headlight aim on 2023 EQE 350 cars with comfort suspension.
issues.next: Get the free headlight software update under recall 23V-853.

issues.t: Roof frame absorbers can come loose in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: There are no symptoms. The risk only shows up in a crash.
issues.why: Energy absorbers in the roof frame may not be secured properly and can break free when the side curtain airbags deploy, striking people inside.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-555. The dealer replaces the absorbers free.

issues.t: Wrong pedestrian warning sound when reversing (recall)
issues.sym: The outside warning sound that electric cars make for pedestrians may sound wrong when the car is in reverse.
issues.why: A software error in the pedestrian sound system plays the wrong reversing sound, which does not meet the federal rule for quiet vehicles.
issues.next: Have the dealer install the sound system software update under recall 25V-366. It is free.

issues.t: Pedestrian warning sound doesn't get louder with speed (recall)
issues.sym: On the AMG EQE SUV, the outside warning sound stays quiet as the car speeds up, so pedestrians may not hear it coming.
issues.why: A software error stops the pedestrian sound from rising in volume with speed.
issues.next: Have the dealer install the free sound system software update under recall 25V-830.

issues.t: Sudden automatic braking with nothing ahead
issues.sym: The car brakes hard and loudly on its own, even with no car or object in front, on local roads or when pulling out of a driveway.
issues.why: The automatic emergency braking system can mistake harmless things for obstacles. Owners have filed government complaints, and driver-assist problems are one of the most common complaint types for the EQE SUV.
issues.next: Report each event to the dealer with the date, time and place so they can read the stored data. Ask for all driver-assist software updates and file a complaint with NHTSA if it continues.

issues.t: Brake pedal goes soft and sinks
issues.sym: After some light braking, pressing harder makes the pedal feel soft and sink, with little extra stopping power.
issues.why: An owner reported this intermittent brake fade to NHTSA. Brake complaints are also one of the most common complaint types filed for the EQE SUV. The cause has not been confirmed by Mercedes.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Treat any soft pedal as urgent. Have the dealer inspect the brakes and read the brake system codes before driving the car normally again.

issues.sym: A "12V battery low" message shows in the car or the Mercedes app, or the car shuts down and won't turn on.
issues.why: The EQE still needs a small 12-volt battery to wake up its computers. On early EQ models the drive battery did not always recharge it while parked. Dealers have fixed this with software updates, charging, or a new 12-volt battery.
issues.next: Plug the car in overnight and see if the warning clears. If it comes back, ask the dealer for software updates and a 12-volt battery test.

issues.sym: Run-flat tires on the 21-inch wheels lose air or blow out, sometimes several times in the first months.
issues.why: The EQE is heavy, and low-profile run-flat tires on large wheels have stiff, short sidewalls that are easily damaged by potholes.
issues.next: Check tire pressures monthly and look for sidewall bulges. Ask the dealer about tire options with a higher load rating, and report repeat failures to NHTSA.

issues.sym: The center screen freezes or lags, phone or sound features act up, or the head unit needs a restart.
issues.why: Software bugs in MBUX. Mercedes has sent many over-the-air and dealer updates for the head unit, MBUX and sound system on 2021–2024 EQE and EQS models.
issues.next: Turn on over-the-air updates. If problems continue, ask the dealer to install all current MBUX and head unit software.

issues.sym: A squeak comes from under the car when backing up slowly, under about 4 mph.
issues.why: A seal in the electric drive unit that separates the coolant from the motor gets wet and squeaks. Mercedes issued a bulletin for it.
issues.next: Not dangerous. Ask the dealer to apply the bulletin repair under warranty.

issues.sym: A rattle or buzz comes from a headrest over bumps.
issues.why: Loose fit between the headrest and its posts. An EQE owner reports it being fixed with felt tape.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to add felt tape or adjust the headrest at your next visit.
